title: Celsus’s inspired nations and the Jews
source_text: Ἑξῆς δὲ τούτοις ἐνθεώτατα ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἔδοξε Κέλσῳ λέγειν ἔθνη Χαλδαίους, ἀφ᾿ ὧν ἡ ἀπατηλὸς γενεθλιαλογία νενέμηται τοὺς ἀνθρώπους. ἀλλὰ καὶ Μάγους τοῖς ἐνθεωτάτοις κατατάττει ἔθνεσιν ὁ Κέλσος, ἀφ᾿ ὧν ἡ παρώνυμος τοῦ ἔθνους αὐτῶν μαγεία καὶ τοῖς λοιποῖς ἔθνεσιν ἐπὶ διαφθορᾷ καὶ ὀλέθρῳ τῶν χρωμένων αὐτῇ ἐπιδεδήμηκε. καὶ Αἰγύπτιοι μὲν ἐν μὲν τοῖς ἀνωτέρω καὶ παρὰ τῷ Κέλσῳ ἐπλανῶντο, ὡς σεμνοὺς μὲν ἔχοντες περιβόλους τῶν νομιζομένων ἱερῶν ἔνδον δὲ οὐδὲν ἀλλ᾿ ἢ πιθήκους ἢ κροκοδείλους ἢ αἶγας ἢ ἀσπίδας ἤ τι τῶν ζῴων· νῦν δὲ ἔδοξε Κέλσῳ ἐνθεώτατον εἰπεῖν καὶ τὸ Αἰγυπτίων ἔθνος, καὶ ἐνθεώτατον ἐξ ἀρχῆς, τάχα ἐπεὶ Ἰουδαίοις ἐξ ἀρχῆς προσπεπολεμήκασι. καὶ Πέρσαι δὲ οἱ τὰς μητέρας γαμοῦντες καὶ θυγατράσι μιγνύμενοι ἔνθεον ἔθνος εἶναι τῷ Κέλσῳ δοκοῦσιν, ἀλλὰ καὶ Ἰνδοὶ, ὧν τινας ἐν τοῖς προειρημένοις ἔλεγε καὶ ἀνθρωπείων γεγεῦσθαι σαρκῶν. μηδὲν δὲ τούτων Ἰουδαίους μάλιστα τοὺς πάλαι πράττοντας οὐ μόνον οὐκ εἶπεν ἐνθεωτάτους ἀλλὰ καὶ αὐτίκα ἀπολουμένους. τοῦτο μὲν ἤδη καὶ ὡς μαντικὸς λέγει περὶ αὐτῶν, οὐχ ὁρῶν πᾶσαν τὴν περὶ Ἰουδαίους καὶ τὴν σεμνὴν πάλαι πολιτείαν αὐτῶν τοῦ θεοῦ οἰκονομίαν, καὶ ὡς „τῷ“ ἐκείνων „παραπτώματι ἡ σωτηρία“ γεγένηται „τοῖς ἔθνεσι“ καὶ „τὸ παράπτωμα αὐτῶν πλοῦτος κόσμου καὶ τὸ ἥττημα αὐτῶν πλοῦτος ἐθνῶν“· ἕως „τὸ πλήρωμα τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰσέλθῃ,“ ἵνα μετὰ τοῦτο „πᾶς,“ ὃν οὐ νοεῖ Κέλσος, „Ἰσραὴλ“ σωθῇ.
pass_a_gloss: Next after these it seemed good to Celsus to name as most inspired (ἐνθεώτατα) nations from the beginning Chaldeans, from whom the deceitful (ἀπατηλός) nativity-casting (γενεθλιαλογία) has been distributed among (νενέμηται) humans. But Celsus also ranks (κατατάττει) Magi among the most inspired nations, from whom the magic (μαγεία) named after (παρώνυμος) their nation has come also to the other nations for corruption (διαφθορᾷ) and destruction (ὀλέθρῳ) of those using it. And Egyptians in the earlier parts even with Celsus were going astray (ἐπλανῶντο), as having stately (σεμνούς) enclosures (περιβόλους) of supposed temples but inside nothing but apes or crocodiles or goats or asps or one of the animals; but now it seemed good to Celsus to call the Egyptian nation also most inspired, and most inspired from the beginning, perhaps since they have warred against (προσπεπολεμήκασι) Jews from the beginning. And Persians who marry (γαμοῦντες) their mothers and mingle with daughters seem to Celsus an inspired (ἔνθεον) nation, and also Indians, of whom he said in the foregoing some had tasted human flesh. Jews, especially those of old, doing none of these, he not only did not call most inspired but also about to perish forthwith (αὐτίκα ἀπολουμένους). This he says about them already also as a diviner (μαντικός), not seeing the whole economy (οἰκονομία) of God concerning the Jews and their venerable former polity (πολιτεία), and how 'by' their 'transgression (παραπτώματι) salvation' has come 'to the Gentiles (ἔθνεσι)' and 'their transgression wealth of the world and their defeat/loss (ἥττημα) wealth of Gentiles', until 'the fullness (πλήρωμα) of the Gentiles enters', so that after this 'all', whom Celsus does not understand (νοεῖ), 'Israel' be saved.
pass_b_english: After this Celsus saw fit to name the Chaldeans among the nations that have been most inspired from the beginning, and it is from them that the deceitful art of casting horoscopes has spread among men. He also ranks the Magi among the most inspired nations, and from them magic, which takes its name from their nation, has spread to the other nations as well, to the ruin and destruction of those who practise it. Earlier, even in Celsus’s own account, the Egyptians were in error, since they have stately precincts around what they consider temples, yet inside there is nothing but apes or crocodiles or goats or asps or some other animal. But now Celsus has seen fit to call the Egyptian nation too most inspired, and most inspired from the beginning, perhaps because they have waged war on the Jews from the beginning. And the Persians, who marry their mothers and lie with their daughters, seem to Celsus an inspired nation; so do the Indians, some of whom, as he said earlier, have even tasted human flesh.

But the Jews, and above all the Jews of old, who did none of these things, he not only did not call most inspired but even said would soon perish. He says this about them now as though he were a diviner as well, not seeing the whole dispensation of God concerning the Jews and their venerable ancient way of life, nor how “through” their “transgression salvation” has come “to the Gentiles” (Romans 11:11), and “their transgression is riches for the world, and their failure riches for the Gentiles” (Romans 11:12), “until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in” (Romans 11:25), so that after this “all Israel,” an Israel Celsus does not understand, “may be saved” (Romans 11:26).

choices.choice: ἐνθεώτατα / ἔνθεον: Celsus’s words for these nations, rendered ‘most inspired’ / ‘inspired’; Origen repeats Celsus’s terms ironically, so they are not put in quotation marks, since the exact wording of Celsus here is reported, not quoted. ἔδοξε Κέλσῳ rendered ‘Celsus saw fit’. γενεθλιαλογία (‘casting nativities’) rendered ‘casting horoscopes’. The Egyptian animal temples refer back to Celsus at 3.17 (checked in the staged Greek); the Indians who eat their fathers to Celsus’s use of Herodotus at 5.34 (checked in the staged Greek). πολιτεία rendered ‘way of life’ (polity, commonwealth). ‘Through their transgression salvation has come to the Gentiles’ follows Romans 11:11 (Origen adds γεγένηται). In Romans 11:26 Origen inserts ‘whom Celsus does not understand’ between ‘all’ and ‘Israel’; kept as an aside in the same place. ‘Diviner’ renders μαντικός, mocking Celsus’s prediction that the Jews would soon perish.

perfects προσπεπολεμήκασι / γεγεῦσθαι rendered 'have waged war' / 'have even tasted'; Indian clause simplified to 'as he said earlier'
notes: earlier loci fixed as 3.17 and 5.34 after checking the staged Greek; 'parenthesis' wording corrected to 'aside'
